Sparse attention cuts the cost of long context by skipping tokens, but it inherits a subtle failure: as the sequence grows, **normalization mass disperses**, so retrieving a handful of relevant facts from hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades. The model still computes attention — it just computes the wrong distribution.

**Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT)** attacks that directly. Instead of the dense $L \times L$ attention matrix, it builds a **linear-size graph over local windows plus $K$ shared hubs**, balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. The hubs act as a small set of global mixing points: a query anywhere in the sequence can reach distant context without touching every token.

Four ingredients make it work. **Bounded-support capacity gating** via simplex sparsemax ($O(L \log L)$) or a sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$) drives excess distractor mass to zero — the whole point, since dilution *is* excess mass. A **three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule** damps the bipartite residuals that plain Sinkhorn leaves behind. An exact **rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint** runs in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 tensor cores, FP32 potentials). And a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant provides verified zero future leakage.

The numbers are striking. On an NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches **97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$** under pure task loss, and 98.83% at $\alpha=0.05$ — matched by the $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU variant. The control matters: with **softmax** gating the same hub OT collapses to **3.52%**. In operator microbenchmarks the kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262K (2.2× faster with 4.0× smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax), and **1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention** at $L=4{,}096$. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval: **100.00% (128/128)** against 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention.

Caveats: multi-layer LM runs still use the unfused path, compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show only modest causal and masked-LM gains, and the 262K number comes from a model trained at $L=128$ extrapolated far beyond its training length.

Source: [arXiv:2611.27951 — Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27951)
